I made the figure: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-leapfrog-personal-projects-claude-skills-unfold/f66a1fc7-f67e-463d-8649-7df90890760b/scratchpad/build/base-nfa/nfa-abcbd.svg`. It shows the NFA at the top and a step-by-step table of active states below it. I rendered it in headless Chrome and checked the image.

Note: the NFA is a smaller form of the usual Thompson construction. I removed ε-states that only connect other ε-states. The language it accepts is the same.

## The NFA

- `q0 --a--> q1` matches the leading `a`.
- From `q1`, three ε-edges go out. An ε-edge moves without reading input. They go to `q2` (the `b` branch), `q4` (the `c` branch) and `q6` (exit the loop).
- `q2 --b--> q3` and `q4 --c--> q5` are the two choices of `(b|c)`.
- `q3` and `q5` go back to `q1` by ε. This is the `*` loop.
- `q6 --d--> q7` matches the final `d`. `q7` is the accept state.

## How it runs

An NFA can be in many states at the same time. The simulator keeps a **set** of active states. For each input symbol it does two things:

1. **Move.** Take every edge from the current set that reads the symbol.
2. **ε-closure.** Add every state that the ε-edges can reach from the result.

The input matches if the set holds the accept state after the last symbol.

| Step | Read | After move | After ε-closure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | (start) | {q0} | {q0} |
| 1 | `a` | {q1} | {q1, q2, q4, q6} |
| 2 | `b` | {q3} | {q1, q2, q3, q4, q6} |
| 3 | `c` | {q5} | {q1, q2, q4, q5, q6} |
| 4 | `b` | {q3} | {q1, q2, q3, q4, q6} |
| 5 | `d` | {q7} | {q7} |

At step 5 only `q6` has a `d` edge, so the set becomes {q7}. `q7` is the accept state, so `"abcbd"` matches.

A failed input works the same way. For `"abx"`, no active state has an `x` edge. The set becomes empty, and the match fails at once.

Each step costs at most one visit per state. That is why this method runs in O(n·m) time and never backtracks. Here n is the input length and m is the number of states.

In the figure, dark cells are the states reached by the move. Light cells are the states added by the ε-closure. The step table above is in Markdown, so you can paste it into your docs under the figure.
